tldr: This is a theme thread, not one event: three weeks of arXiv papers proposing new agent benchmarks, starting with multi-agent decision and coordination tests (TandemBench, WorkflowArena). Later papers moved to MCP hallucination, memory poisoning, and long-horizon real-world tasks such as AI infra tuning and research sessions.
whats_new: REPA (Nov 23) models how one agent's local errors propagate into system-level failures across multi-agent workflows, two days after MASSys showed Star vs Chain topology rankings flip under KV-cache pressure.
why_it_matters: Multi-agent scores now depend on serving substrate and error propagation, not just the model, so a leaderboard number may not hold on your own inference stack.

beats.headline: Benchmarks target how agents divide work and coordinate
beats.summary: Decision models, workflow orchestration, shared-memory coordination, and full-duplex voice task handling each get a dedicated test.

beats.headline: Tool calls, memory, and multi-turn state come under test
beats.summary: MCP hallucinations, memory poisoning across sessions, and user-state tracking over turns; two memory papers sit at the theme's edge.

beats.headline: Long-horizon, real-world task benchmarks multiply
beats.summary: AI infra optimization, live research workspaces, privacy-aware code review, multi-arm robot control, video, and spatial exploration.

beats.headline: The system layer: serving substrate and error propagation
beats.summary: Papers now measure what happens around the agents: batch scheduling, serving load, and how local errors cascade.

open_questions: Does MASSys's topology-ranking flip under KV-cache pressure reproduce on other serving stacks?
Does REPA's error-propagation model hold beyond the three Qwen base models it was evaluated on?
Do any of these benchmarks release harnesses that teams adopt for their own regression evals?
Does MCPHallu's separation of reasoning, execution, and memory hallucinations show up in vendor MCP agent evaluations?
take_for_builders: Before choosing a multi-agent topology from a published score, rerun the comparison on your own serving stack at production load, because MASSys shows the ranking can flip with KV-cache pressure.
